The Civil Procedure Code grants exemption to Rulers from being sued. Exemption from being sued is not personal liberty within the meaning of Article 21. Exemption from being sued is procedural advantage which will no longer be available. Again, s. 197 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is a procedural advantage. In all these cases the petitioner cannot complain in this Court because the position is derived from the recognition of Rulership and Art. 363 is an insurmountable and impenetrable bar. Recognition of Rulership is not a legal right. It is not a right to property. Privy purse is not a legal right to property. There is no fundamental right to privy purse. There is no fundamental right to Rulership.
